digest.component_or_area: plan-review criterion registration and container pass
propositions: Plan-review acceptance criteria across an epic and its children can be mutually unsatisfiable, surfacing contradictions only at implementation or verification gates, forcing full LLM re-review each time.

A new 1-TURN criterion ac-satisfiability (facet coherence) must own the concern of whether a ticket's AC and Scope/Out-of-Scope declarations are jointly satisfiable, covering universal-vs-carve-out, derived-artifact closure, and snapshot cardinality contradiction shapes.

The G3 child-coverage audit cannot fire because the sibling roster it receives contains only ticket ids and titles, lacking the acceptance-criteria items needed to test coverage; the roster must be enriched by extracting AC items from each child.

The sibling roster is currently built by three independent copies of the same expression in pass1.py, fidelity_spot_eval.py, and eval_solver.py; they must be unified into a single shared build_sibling_roster helper to prevent divergence between production and eval harnesses.

The rendered roster must be moved from per-pairing instructions into the byte-stable system-prompt prefix, sent once rather than repeated, and its token cost must be included in the parent_tokens prefix estimate for correct bin-packing and warm-cache gating.

The ac-satisfiability criterion ships as advisory at default 0.95 posture; it does not change existing Pass-2 verifier axes or G3's posture/threshold, which are deferred pending dogfooding data from this change.
